metadata.subject: Battery Electric Vehicle Diagnostic and Rectification
metadata.description: BEV diagnostic fault code scenarios for KT/KA practice — covers battery, BMS, drivetrain, and thermal systems

diagnosis_steps: Connect OBD-II scanner and read DTCs
Check individual cell voltages via BMS data stream
Identify cells with voltage deviation >50mV from average
Measure cell temperature differentials across pack
Review charge/discharge cycle history in BMS memory

symptoms: No communication with BMS on diagnostic bus
diagnosis_steps: Verify 12V supply to BMS control module
Check CAN bus communication on BMS network
Inspect BMS harness for open circuits or shorts
Test BMS ground connections
Replace BMS module if hardware fault confirmed

symptoms: Power output limited by thermal protection
diagnosis_steps: Check coolant level in battery thermal circuit
Inspect coolant pump operation and flow rate
Measure battery pack inlet/outlet coolant temperatures
Check for coolant leaks at hose connections
Verify thermostat and chiller operation
Read motor controller DTCs with OEM scanner
Check HV bus voltage at inverter input
Measure phase current balance across motor windings
Inspect motor temperature sensor readings
Check motor resolver/encoder signal integrity

symptoms: Vehicle may not start after parking
diagnosis_steps: Measure 12V battery voltage with engine running (expect 13.5-14.5V)
Check DC-DC converter HV input voltage
Verify DC-DC converter enable signal from VCU
Measure DC-DC output current under load
Inspect HV connector at DC-DC converter for corrosion

symptoms: Vehicle unable to activate Ready mode
Clicking sound from battery pack area
diagnosis_steps: Check main positive and negative contactor coil resistance
Verify pre-charge contactor and resistor function
Measure HV bus voltage before and after contactors
Inspect contactor wiring harness for damage
Test contactor activation with bi-directional control
Read current sensor value in BMS data stream at rest (should be near 0A)
Apply known current load and compare sensor reading
Check Hall-effect sensor supply voltage (typically 5V)
Inspect current sensor signal wire for interference
Replace current sensor if offset error exceeds +/-2A at rest

symptoms: Battery temperature reading out of range
diagnosis_steps: Read all battery temperature sensor values in BMS data stream
Compare readings — sensors within pack should be within 5 degrees C
Check NTC thermistor resistance vs temperature curve
Inspect sensor connectors inside battery pack
Replace individual NTC sensors if resistance deviation confirmed
Check coolant pump relay and fuse
Verify pump power supply voltage
Test pump manually via bi-directional control on scanner
Measure pump current draw (compare to spec)
Inspect pump impeller for blockage

symptoms: Vehicle shuts down in rain or wet conditions
diagnosis_steps: Disconnect HV battery following HV service procedures
Use 500V insulation resistance tester on HV cables
Minimum acceptable: 500 kOhm (1 MOhm preferred)
Inspect HV cable routing for chafe points
Check orange HV cable connectors for moisture ingress
Read OBC-specific DTCs with OEM scanner
Check AC input voltage at OBC (should match grid: 220V +/-10%)
Verify charge port contact resistance (<0.1 Ohm)
Check pilot signal (CP) voltage and PWM duty cycle
Test OBC outlet DC voltage to battery

symptoms: Abnormal motor temperature rise under light load
diagnosis_steps: Measure motor winding resistance per phase (should be balanced)
Perform insulation resistance test on motor windings
Check motor temperature sensor against known ambient
Inspect motor cooling circuit flow rate
Review motor thermal model data in VCU
Read inverter DTCs and freeze frame data
Check IGBT gate driver voltage levels
Measure inverter output phase voltages
Verify inverter coolant temperature and flow
Test IGBT modules for short circuit (with HV disconnected)

symptoms: CAN communication errors across multiple networks
diagnosis_steps: Download all DTCs from all control modules
Check CAN bus network topology and termination resistance
Verify VCU power supply and ground quality
Update VCU firmware if calibration mismatch detected
Inspect VCU connector for moisture or corrosion

symptoms: Battery unable to cool in hot ambient
Charging speed reduced above 35 degrees C ambient
AC system pressure faults linked to battery chiller
Thermal runaway risk in extreme heat
diagnosis_steps: Check refrigerant pressure in battery chiller circuit
Verify chiller valve operation and opening
Measure refrigerant temperature drop across chiller
Check compressor output when chiller is demanded
Inspect refrigerant lines for leaks using UV dye test

symptoms: All battery parameters show default values
diagnosis_steps: Measure CAN bus high/low voltage (expected: H=2.5-3.5V, L=1.5-2.5V)
Check CAN termination resistance (should be ~60 Ohm between H and L)
Locate and inspect CAN harness for damage at flex points
Test CAN bus with oscilloscope for signal quality
Check BMS module for internal communication fault

symptoms: Vehicle fails to wake from sleep mode
DC-DC converter compensating at maximum output
diagnosis_steps: Measure 12V battery voltage (key off, key on, Ready mode)
Load test 12V battery at rated CCA
Check 12V battery age and cycle count
Measure DC-DC converter output voltage stability
Verify 12V battery venting and charging connections

symptoms: Cell voltage spread >100mV after full charge
One module charges/discharges faster than others
diagnosis_steps: Read individual cell voltages in BMS data stream
Identify cells or modules with persistent high/low deviation
Check passive balancing resistors for continuity
Verify balancing is active during charge (BMS should balance top-of-charge)
Assess if deviation indicates cell degradation requiring replacement

symptoms: SOC does not return to 100% after full charge
BMS shows different SOC from expected based on energy consumed
Sudden range anxiety at moderate SOC
diagnosis_steps: Perform full charge cycle and record SOC at charger cutoff
Run discharge test comparing BMS SOC to actual energy out
Check current sensor calibration
Verify BMS software version and SOC algorithm calibration
Perform battery capacity test (full charge-discharge cycle measurement)

symptoms: Vehicle fails to enter Ready mode
Loud contactor click followed by immediate disconnect
Capacitor bank voltage not rising during pre-charge
diagnosis_steps: Measure pre-charge resistor value (compare to spec: typically 10-100 Ohm)
Monitor HV bus capacitor voltage during pre-charge attempt
Check pre-charge contactor for welding or failure to close
Calculate expected pre-charge time constant (RC)
Inspect for HV loads that may be drawing current during pre-charge

symptoms: Coolant leak detected inside battery enclosure
Battery pack weight increase from water ingress
Intermittent faults after rain or car wash
diagnosis_steps: Inspect battery pack enclosure seal with pressure test (5 kPa)
Check drain plugs and vent valves for blockage
Use borescope to inspect inside battery pack for moisture
Measure insulation resistance after drying pack (should exceed 1 MOhm)
Replace compromised seals and gaskets per OEM specification
